name: PostHog
summary: A product suite presented as a place to explore, rather than a stack of interchangeable cards.

observations.hero: A desktop-like shell surrounds a central window. Navigation icons sit on both sides; the introduction and signup panel share a row.
observations.typography: Bold compact sans-serif headings; body text stays conversational. Colored inline highlights reinforce key terms.
observations.visual_system: Green illustrated environment, translucent pale window, orange beveled actions and vividly colored story tabs.
observations.page_sequence: Introduction → illustrative product tabs → tool inventory → customers → data warehouse → pricing → company rationale → reading → deliberately playful closing CTA.
observations.interaction: Clicked Ship with PostHog. The selected tab and product story changed, with sample inbox reports replacing the earlier assistant story. A pause control was present but not tested.
observations.accessibility: Semantic structure inspected through browser accessibility output. No contrast, keyboard, screen-reader or reduced-motion audit was completed.

principles: Give a broad suite a navigable mental model.
Let expressive brand elements organize information instead of merely decorating it.
Identify illustrative data as illustrative.
interpretation.fit: Choose this approach only if it explains the audience’s actual evaluation task.
interpretation.risks: Desktop chrome competes for attention; nested scrolling needs separate mobile and keyboard testing.

limitations: Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
Exact font names, animation timing and implementation libraries were not verified.
Tablet, mobile and reduced-motion behavior remain unverified.

name: Resend
summary: Editorial type and generous silence open a long, increasingly concrete product tour for developer email infrastructure.

observations.hero: At 1363 × 936, a left-aligned two-line serif headline moves from bright white to gray on black; Get started and Documentation sit beneath the brief explanation. A faint light ray gives the largely open right side a focal point. A slim navigation bar stays at the top while scrolling.
observations.typography: High-contrast display serif paired with plain sans-serif body and monospace code. Exact families unverified.
observations.visual_system: Black surfaces, white display text, subtle lighting and finely outlined code panels. The integration chapter uses a large envelope symbol and a centered gradient-accented heading before the language chooser. Wide negative space alternates with dense product windows, making the change in information density intentional.
observations.page_sequence: Full-page desktop scan: open hero → customer logos → integration code window → paired Test mode and Modular webhooks → Editor demo → contacts and analytics pair → React Email code and preview → deliverability grid → single testimonial → dashboard controls → testimonial carousel → large serif closing statement and footer. The page is roughly 12,352 px tall in this captured viewport; the exact length depends on browser rendering.
observations.interaction: Clicked Python in the integration code chooser. The main language and nested example tabs both selected Python, and the visible snippet changed to Python. The dashboard tabs and testimonial carousel were seen in the full-page capture but were not operated. No email was sent.
observations.accessibility: Semantic structure inspected through browser accessibility output. No contrast, keyboard, screen-reader or reduced-motion audit was completed.

principles: Make technical adoption concrete with a short, relevant integration example.
A quiet hero can precede dense functional explanation.
Use typographic contrast to create identity without obscuring product meaning.
interpretation.fit: Choose this approach only if it explains the audience’s actual evaluation task.
interpretation.risks: Some body text appears subdued against black. The long sequence and dense product windows demand careful small-screen pacing. A full-page capture does not establish the behavior of unclicked tabs or carousels.

limitations: Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
Exact font names, animation timing and implementation libraries were not verified.
Tablet, mobile and reduced-motion behavior remain unverified.

Hero, middle and footer regions plus a full-page desktop capture were visually inspected; the Python control was operated. Other interactive controls, keyboard and assistive-technology behavior were not tested.

name: LightSprint

viewports.desktop: 1363 × 936: rendered hero, full-page scan, selected sections and interaction

summary: A collaborative agent workflow staged as an orange-and-charcoal product scene, from request to review.

observations.hero: Centered two-line sans heading and paired Book demo / Start for free actions sit above a broad orange, charcoal and gray textured field. A sample task composer and task boards animate over that field. A narrow announcement strip and sticky dark navigation frame the opening.
observations.typography: Large plain sans headings carry the argument; compact labels, monospaced task details and code snippets distinguish product states. Exact families unverified.
observations.visual_system: Near-black backdrop, vivid orange actions and grainy orange-gray atmospheric panels. Live-looking task windows recur against the same textured world; an integration grid and model picker give dense sections a more utilitarian rhythm.
observations.page_sequence: Hero and animated task boards → five-step Now everyone can ship sequence → existing-stack integrations and model picker → walkthrough → shared skills/context/session → role-specific use cases → testimonials → FAQ → closing action and footer. A full-page capture left large scroll-triggered regions dark until traversed, so lower sections were also checked through rendered page state and targeted scrolling.
observations.interaction: Clicked Automated QA and testing in the five-step sequence. Its selected indicator moved and the adjacent scene changed to a QA panel listing a merge conflict, potential security issues and design-guideline warning. No task was submitted. The scene also advanced as the page scrolled.
observations.accessibility: The sequence exposes named buttons and the FAQ exposes expandable buttons in the accessibility tree. No keyboard, screen-reader or motion-preference test was performed.

principles: Stage a complex process as a sequence of decisions and visible artifacts.
Reuse a coherent product world across hero, walkthrough and proof.
Distinguish illustrative task states from a live execution claim.
interpretation.fit: Best for collaborative tools whose buyer must understand handoffs between roles and code review.
interpretation.risks: Long scroll-linked scenes can obscure content when a capture does not trigger reveal states. Decorative task chrome and dense low-contrast labels need separate small-screen and accessibility review.

limitations: One cloud Chromium session at a 1363 × 936 desktop viewport; the site can change after this date.
Tablet, mobile, keyboard-only, screen-reader, color contrast and reduced-motion behavior were not tested.
Exact font families, animation timing, implementation details and conversion effects were not independently established.
Some lower visuals were visible in the rendered DOM or after scrolling, but not all animation states were exercised. Testimonials and model support are company statements, not independently verified.

name: Palette

viewports.desktop: 1363 × 936: rendered hero, full-page scan, selected sections and interaction

summary: A changing media stage leads into a long, modular explanation of generation, editing and model choice.

observations.hero: White navigation surrounds a nearly full-viewport dark media canvas. Large white sans type overlays glossy abstract footage near the lower left; purple Book a call and outlined Explore actions sit on the lower right. The short verb in the headline changes with the selected clip.
observations.typography: Oversized, heavy sans display for the opening and section headlines; narrow uppercase micro-labels and light body copy establish pace. Exact font families unverified.
observations.visual_system: White and pale lavender page surfaces, black media frames, violet accents and thin hand-drawn connector marks. Alternating image/text pairs lead through capabilities; purple large-scale graphic fields separate the model and pipeline chapters. Several embedded media panels reported Unable to play media in this browser.
observations.page_sequence: Video hero → backer/creator trust row → industry cards → Cut/Flow product demos → Generate/Edit/Storyboard/Characters alternating chapters → example carousel → model accordion → production pipeline → impact controls → API code samples → individual/enterprise tiers → closing video and footer.

name: Cyclon

viewports.desktop: 1363 × 936: rendered hero, full-page scan, selected sections and interaction

summary: A short waitlist page uses a single phone image and three plain-language capabilities to introduce a new device.

observations.hero: Centered, bold two-line statement on white with brief explanatory copy, an email waitlist form and YC backing directly beneath. A tall front-view phone image extends below the fold; navigation is only the logo and About us.
observations.typography: Black heavy sans display and smaller gray sans body; the few section labels are much quieter than the hero. Exact family unverified.
observations.visual_system: Monochrome white/black with an orange YC accent and a metallic device render. Wide whitespace keeps the page short; no card system or elaborate gradient is used.
observations.page_sequence: Hero statement and waitlist → phone render → three short capability columns (build apps, connect services, delegate across apps) → concluding belief statement → sparse About/Privacy/Terms/Contact footer.
observations.interaction: Opened About us from the header; navigation reached /about and displayed founders and background. The waitlist form was visible but no email was entered or submitted. No product demonstration was available on the homepage.
observations.accessibility: The waitlist input has an accessible Email address label, and there is a Skip to content link. Submission behavior, error messaging, keyboard traversal and screen-reader behavior were not tested.

principles: Use a single clear action when the product is still collecting interest.
Give a new hardware concept a recognizable physical anchor.
Keep early claims proportionate to what a page can show.
interpretation.fit: Useful for a prelaunch device where the immediate user decision is whether to join a waitlist.
interpretation.risks: The page leaves product reality, availability and proof largely unanswered. A phone render and capability statements are not evidence of a functioning device.

limitations: One cloud Chromium session at a 1363 × 936 desktop viewport; the site can change after this date.
Tablet, mobile, keyboard-only, screen-reader, color contrast and reduced-motion behavior were not tested.
Exact font families, animation timing, implementation details and conversion effects were not independently established.
No email was submitted; form validation and confirmation remain unverified. The page has no product interaction to operate beyond navigation.
